english.title: Views / accesses a document / record on the internet containing information useful to terrorism

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Counter Terrorism and Border Security Act 2019

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonable excuse, viewed or otherwise accessed by means of the internet a document or record containing information of a kind likely to be useful to a person committing or preparing an act of terrorism, namely **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF INFORMATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 58(1)(c) and (4) of the Terrorism Act 2000.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Attorney General is required, see section 117 of the Terrorism Act 2000.
(ii) In this section 'record' includes a photographic or electronic record.
(iii) As per section 58(3), it is a defence for a person charged with an offence under this section to prove that he had a reasonable excuse for his action or possession.
(iv) Terrorism is defined in section 1 of the Terrorism Act 2000.

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: Maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Maximum 15 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
